_comment: Fragment 89 — D-133: an identity field's role reasoned from what would make an already-decided window meaningless if it were excluded, and defaults offered only where the answer already followed from a fact already on record. Merged 2026-08-25.

nodes.label: A Field's Role Reasoned From What Would Make an Already-Decided Window Meaningless
nodes.description: Whether an identity hash should include free-form framing text was settled by checking what would happen to an already-ruled eligibility window if it did: a hash sensitive to framing would let every resubmission escape the window it was built to gate, so the window's own prior ruling determined the hash's composition without a new business input.
nodes.rationale: A technical design question can sometimes be closed by tracing its consequence back through an already-ratified decision rather than by asking for new input. Finding the field composition that keeps the existing eligibility window meaningful is a stronger justification than an arbitrary implementation choice would have been.

nodes.label: Recommended Defaults Offered Only Where an Existing Fact Already Answered the Question
nodes.description: Three of five business-facing questions asking who holds a given authority were given suggested answers because the one-person operating model already on record answered the who directly, while the two questions carrying real numeric business-risk judgment were left with no suggestion at all.
nodes.rationale: Offering a default is only safe where the answer is already implied by a fact the business itself established, not where it would substitute Lane A's judgment for a risk-bearing decision. The split between defaulted and non-defaulted items is the boundary between reducing a decision-maker's workload and quietly making the decision for them.
